sourceFile: "2026 Diocesan Cycle of Prayer, July through September 2026" -- a one-page PDF supplied directly by Josh, since the diocese's own resource page (https://dioceseofeaston.org/communications/cycle-of-prayer/) only links to PDFs whose direct download URLs could not be located in the raw HTML from this session's sandbox.
notes: This is a quarterly document (July-September 2026 only) -- the diocese's own resource page, per this corpus's roster research, noted 'latest quarter ends September 30. Recheck for Q4' -- consistent with this corpus's other quarterly-published sources (see Missouri, Springfield's own roster note). Not a gap in transcription; a Q4 2026 quarter, if/when published, would extend this same file.

Every entry is prose, not a clean 'Congregation, Town' table -- subjects are extracted from each week's own sentence. `parish` is used only where the source explicitly names both a congregation and its town; a named person, committee, staff group, or a congregation with no town given is recorded as `category`.

September 13: "Christ Church, I.U., Worton" is transcribed with `name` "Christ Church, I.U." and `place` "Worton" -- "I.U." is preserved as printed (a historical designation some Maryland Eastern Shore parishes carry, not a transcription artifact), splitting on the LAST comma rather than the first so it stays part of the congregation's own name.

August 23: "Green Hill Church" is recorded as `category` rather than `parish` -- the source names no separate town for it ("Green Hill" reads as part of the church's own name, not a disclosed place), so no `place` is fabricated.

September 20 names two of the Rev. Dr. Darcy Williams's congregations in one sentence -- "Augustine Parish, Chesapeake City" (a place is given) and "the Church of the Good Shepherd" (no place given) -- split into a `parish` subject for the former and a `category` subject for the latter, plus a separate `category` subject for Williams and her spouse.

September 6 names two distinct subjects in one sentence (a bishop being remembered, and a separate diocesan-wide ministry) -- split into two `category` subjects rather than kept as one, since each names something genuinely distinct.
No entry carries a liturgical Sunday label in the source, so `liturgicalNote` is null throughout.
